correctness.rationale: The fixed locus is explicitly the simplex on n even-column orbit-pair midpoints. The precise published wedge theorem gives rank-two free integral H_n and no other reduced homology. After barycentric subdivision, nonfixed relative cells occur in free involution pairs, giving a bounded complex of free Z[C2]-modules. Derived tensor and the two-periodic C2 resolution force vanishing of all positive group Tor; Lefschetz trace zero and classification of rank-two involution lattices force the regular module. Thus the geometric quotient has integral sphere homology, with no torsion. Armstrong and Hurewicz–Whitehead give S^n for n>=2; the n=1 quotient has an explicit checked six-pair collapse onto a connected unicyclic graph. Exhaustive finite samples independently check the face/fixed-space definitions and small quotient boundaries.

value.rationale: The natural all-length geometric row-symmetry quotient of the recently studied finite hexagonal-chain independence family receives a complete integral homotopy classification, not just rational traces or the ordinary wedge rank. The regular integral lattice and resulting absence of two-torsion remove a structural obstruction not visible to previous character formulas. The uniform theorem includes the base circle and infinitely many higher spheres and gives a motivated illustration of how stabilizer geometry controls orbit topology.
